I want to use a widely available quantised version of Gemma 4 32B in the Kaggle dual T4 GPU environment. It would be great if it could be run using vLLM. The main purpose is to perform OCR on Bengali images. I have a dataset ready with the individual pages of 3 PDFs organised as images.

Gemma 4 32B release

Gemma 4 31B AWQ quantized vLLM support

Evaluated hardware constraints and model compatibility feasibility.

Done

Short answer: Yes, it's possible, but it'll be tight on dual T4s.

Some quick context — Gemma 4 released in April 2026 (after my training cutoff, so I searched for current details rather than relying on memory). Key facts relevant to your plan:

Sizes are E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B-A4B (MoE), and 31B (dense) — there's no exact "32B," but 31B dense is what you're thinking of.

AWQ 4-bit checkpoints exist and are vLLM-ready, e.g. QuantTrio/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ and cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit (~20.5 GB on disk).

vLLM support is real, via --tensor-parallel-size 2 --quantization awq (or compressed-tensors for the QAT checkpoints).

It's natively multimodal (text+image), so OCR is a supported use case.

Caveats for your specific setup (Kaggle dual T4, 16 GB each ≈ 32 GB total):

20.5 GB of weights split across TP=2 leaves a fairly thin margin for KV cache + activations + vision tower overhead, especially since Kaggle usually gives you a bit under 16 GB usable per GPU.

T4 is Turing-generation — no native bf16 tensor cores and no fp8 support, so you're constrained to fp16 execution and can't use fp8 KV cache tricks that newer GPUs get. There are already reported quirks with Gemma 4's heterogeneous attention head dims on non-Blackwell/non-Hopper hardware.

The QAT w4a16 checkpoints (Google's official quantized release, ~66% smaller than BF16) might be a safer bet than AWQ for stability, but I haven't confirmed T4 compatibility for those either.

The 26B-A4B MoE variant is also worth considering — similar storage footprint but far fewer active params per token, so likely faster if VRAM allows.

Given the tight margins, this is doable but will probably need careful tuning of --max-model-len, --gpu-memory-utilization, and possibly --max-num-seqs 1 to avoid OOM.

Ready for your next instructions — happy to help set up the vLLM serving config, test a smaller variant first, or work through the OCR pipeline once you confirm direction.

Answer briefly — do I need to set max_model_len this high?

Weighed token allocation across image encoding and text output.

Weighed token allocation across image encoding and text output.

Brief answer: probably not necessary, but it depends on how dense the pages are.

Your real budget per request is: image tokens (from the vision encoder) + prompt (~60 tokens) + output (up to 4096 tokens for max_tokens). At MAX_IMAGE_SIDE=1600, a full page image with Gemma 4's dynamic-resolution vision tower could easily use 1000–3000+ image tokens, so a dense Bengali page could realistically approach 5000–6000 tokens total.

8192 gives you headroom, but if your pages aren't extremely text-dense, you could likely drop to 4096 and free up VRAM for a larger CHUNK_SIZE or more KV cache — which matters more on T4s than having margin you're not using.

Cheapest way to know for sure: check result.outputs[0].token_ids length (or usage) on your validation run — if actual usage is well under 4096, shrink max_model_len accordingly.

Why did this error occur?

Assistant:

8/5/2026 23:33:58

Diagnosed hardware incompatibility between kernel requirements and GPU capabilities.

Diagnosed hardware incompatibility between kernel requirements and GPU capabilities.

Done

The crash's real root cause is this line:

triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 98304, Hardware limit: 65536

What's happening: T4 is a Turing-generation GPU with a hard limit of 64 KB (65536 bytes) of shared memory per streaming multiprocessor. Gemma 4's attention implementation uses heterogeneous head dimensions — local sliding-window layers use head_dim=256, but the global attention layers use head_dim=512 (this showed up in the vLLM GitHub issue I found earlier too). vLLM's Triton fused-attention kernel needs 96 KB of shared memory to handle that larger global head dimension in one block — 50% more than T4 physically has.

This is a hardware ceiling, not a config problem. Newer GPUs (A100: 164 KB, H100: 228 KB) clear this easily; T4 can't, period. Lowering max_model_len, max_num_seqs, or gpu_memory_utilization won't help — this happens during kernel compilation/CUDA graph capture, before any of those budgets come into play.

(There's also a libnvrtc.so.13: cannot open shared object file warning in the log — that's a separate, non-fatal issue about a missing CUDA runtime compilation library that only affects an optional deep_gemm fast path. It's not what killed the run.)

Likely fixes worth trying, roughly in order of effort:

Force a different attention backend that doesn't hit this shared-memory ceiling on Turing — e.g. set VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=XFORMERS (or FLASHINFER if available) before launching, since xFormers' memory-efficient attention doesn't need the same large fused block.

Add enforce_eager=True to skip CUDA graph capture — this may dodge the capture-time failure, though the same kernel could still fail on first real forward pass since the limit is per-call, not just per-capture.

If neither works, this may mean Gemma 4 31B's attention path isn't currently viable on T4 at all via vLLM, and you'd want to fall back to the 26B-A4B MoE variant (worth checking if it has the same head_dim asymmetry) or a Gemma 3 27B checkpoint instead, which predates this architecture change.

Good catch — and the log tells us why the previous fix failed. Two things happened:

Unknown vLLM environment variable detected: VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND — this vLLM version (0.26.0, note it's newer than the 0.19 the model card assumed) doesn't recognize that env var name/mechanism the way older vLLM did.

More importantly: Gemma4 model has heterogeneous head dimensions (head_dim=256, global_head_dim=512). FA4 not available, forcing TRITON_ATTN backend. — this is model-specific logic inside vLLM itself, hardcoded in config.py. When it detects Gemma 4's mixed head dimensions and no FlashAttention-4 support (FA4 needs Hopper/Blackwell), it unconditionally overrides to TRITON_ATTN — regardless of what backend you request via env var. Our xFormers override never had a chance to take effect.

So this isn't a config problem I can route around with an env var — it's vLLM deciding for you, specifically because this hardware/model combination has no FA4 path. And that forced Triton kernel is the one needing 96 KB of shared memory that T4 (64 KB limit) can't provide.

On enforce_eager: worth ruling out, but I don't expect it to help — the crash happens inside the Triton kernel's own compilation (triton.compiler.errors / OutOfResources), not in CUDA graph machinery. Eager mode skips graph capture, but the same kernel would still get invoked (just later, on the first real forward pass) and would likely fail identically. Still cheap to test if you want to confirm that empirically before we move on.

My honest read: this looks like Gemma 4 31B's attention path may not currently be viable on T4 via this vLLM version, full stop — not a tunable parameter problem. Given that, the productive paths forward are:

Check whether the 26B-A4B MoE variant has the same head_dim=512 global-attention layers (if not, it might sidestep this entirely).

Fall back to Gemma 3 27B, which predates this hybrid-head-dimension architecture and has well-established T4/vLLM compatibility.

Try VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN (old FA2, not FA4) as a long shot, in case that specific override path checks for FA4-vs-FA2 rather than FA-vs-Triton — but I'd rate this low-probability given the log's phrasing suggests an unconditional force.

Diagnosed configuration API change rather than quantization issue.

vLLM Gemma 4 T4 "shared memory" "Hardware limit: 65536" triton_attn

Diagnosed configuration API change rather than quantization issue.

Done

Root cause: not your quantization choice — it's a vLLM API break. VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND env var is deprecated/no-op as of vLLM 0.13.0+ (replaced by AttentionConfig / --attention-backend). Your log confirms it: Unknown vLLM environment variable detected: VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND. So vLLM silently ignored your override, fell back to auto-selection, picked TRITON_ATTN for Gemma 4's head_dim=512 global-attention layers, and that kernel needs 98,304B of shared memory — over T4's 65,536B hardware ceiling. Same failure your code comment already anticipated, just via a different mechanism (config API, not env var).

Fix — pass the backend through the LLM() constructor instead of the env var:

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.config import AttentionConfig
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum

# delete/comment this — it no longer does anything:
# os.environ["VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND"] = "XFORMERS"

llm = LLM(
    model=cfg["model"],
    quantization=cfg["quantization"],
    dtype="float16",
    tensor_parallel_size=cfg["tensor_parallel_size"],
    max_model_len=cfg["max_model_len"],
    gpu_memory_utilization=cfg["gpu_memory_utilization"],
    trust_remote_code=True,
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
    enforce_eager=ENFORCE_EAGER,
    attention_config=AttentionConfig(backend=AttentionBackendEnum.XFORMERS),
    # equivalently: attention_backend="XFORMERS"
)

XFORMERS is still a valid v1 backend (vllm/v1/attention/backends/xformers.py exists in current vLLM), and it doesn't hit the Triton shared-memory ceiling since it isn't a Triton-JIT kernel. FLASH_ATTN/FA4 aren't options here regardless — they require sm80+ (Ampere), and T4 is sm75 (Turing), which your log's FA4 not available line already confirms.

If XFORMERS also fails to install/import cleanly in the Kaggle image, TORCH_SDPA is the other safe fallback for Turing (slower, but always works — no custom kernel compilation).

No need to switch to a different quant (AWQ is fine) or an Unsloth checkpoint — this isn't a weights/quantization problem, it's purely the attention-kernel selection on T4. Re-run cell 3 with this change; you don't need to touch cells 4 onward.

vLLM AttentionBackendEnum members list "TORCH_SDPA" "TRITON_ATTN" "FLEX_ATTENTION" registry.py

vllm/vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py at main · vllm-project/vllm (github.com)

Investigated vLLM backend compatibility issues and identified downgrade solutions.

Done

XFORMERS is gone — not renamed, actually removed. I checked the current registry source directly: AttentionBackendEnum in this vLLM build has no XFORMERS member at all. Full list of CUDA-relevant options: FLASH_ATTN, FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV, TRITON_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV, FLASHINFER, FLASHINFER_MLA, FLEX_ATTENTION, NO_ATTENTION, TORCH_SDPA (present as an enum tag but its class path is "" — it's a ViT-only marker now, not a usable decoder backend; calling get_class() on it raises must be registered before use).

This matters because Turing (T4, sm75) genuinely lost backend support in recent vLLM: FLASH_ATTN/FLASHINFER need sm80+ (Ampere), TRITON_ATTN is what's already blowing your shared-memory budget, and TORCH_SDPA/XFORMERS — the two things that used to rescue Turing — are both gone from the decoder attention path. There's an open, unresolved vLLM issue (#29743, filed Nov 2025) about exactly this: no working attention backend for Turing GPUs on models with this kind of head config.

Two real paths forward:

1. Try FLEX_ATTENTION first (least work, might just work):

attention_config=AttentionConfig(backend=AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION)

It's PyTorch-native (torch.nn.attention.flex_attention), not a hand-tuned Triton kernel with a hardcoded 512-head-dim tile, so it may not hit the same shared-memory ceiling. Not guaranteed on sm75 — test it before committing to a full run.

2. If that fails, pin an older vLLM that predates the Turing regression, rather than fighting the current backend registry:

# !pip install -q "vllm==0.10.2" "transformers==5.5.0" pillow tqdm

That's roughly the last generation where XFORMERS/TORCH_SDPA were still live, first-class decoder backends — the people you've seen running Gemma 4 31B on Kaggle T4s without issue are almost certainly on an older pinned vLLM, not main/latest. You'd go back to your original os.environ["VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND"] = "XFORMERS" approach, since that env var still worked pre-0.13.0.

I'd try (1) in a fresh kernel restart first since it's zero-install-cost; fall back to (2) if FLEX_ATTENTION also errors on the head_dim=512 layers. Not a quantization/checkpoint problem either way — AWQ vs. Unsloth won't touch this.

Right — 0.10.2 predates Gemma 4 entirely (added in v0.19.0, needs transformers>=5.5.0). Downgrading that far throws away model support. My mistake for not checking that boundary before suggesting a blind downgrade.

Rather than keep guessing version boundaries, check what's actually available in whatever vLLM you have installed before restarting anything:

from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum
print([b.name for b in AttentionBackendEnum])

I pulled the current registry source directly (vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py, main branch) and confirmed: XFORMERS doesn't exist as an enum member anymore, period — not renamed, fully removed. Full CUDA-relevant list: FLASH_ATTN, FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV, TRITON_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN_DIFFKV, FLASHINFER, FLASHINFER_MLA, FLEX_ATTENTION, NO_ATTENTION, TORCH_SDPA (present but empty class path — "this tag is only used for ViT," not selectable for the decoder). FLASH_ATTN/FLASHINFER need sm80+ (Ampere), so they're off the table for your T4s regardless.

That leaves FLEX_ATTENTION as the only remaining candidate on your current (0.26.0) install — worth trying before any downgrade, since it costs you nothing:

from vllm.config import AttentionConfig
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum

llm = LLM(
    model=cfg["model"],
    quantization=cfg["quantization"],
    dtype="float16",
    tensor_parallel_size=cfg["tensor_parallel_size"],
    max_model_len=cfg["max_model_len"],
    gpu_memory_utilization=cfg["gpu_memory_utilization"],
    trust_remote_code=True,
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
    attention_config=AttentionConfig(backend=AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION),
)

If it also fails on the head_dim=512 layers (FlexAttention is Triton-templated under the hood too, so it's not guaranteed to dodge the same shared-memory ceiling), the next thing to actually try is pinning to vllm==0.19.0 specifically — the exact release that first added Gemma 4 — and running the diagnostic print above to see if XFORMERS was still registered at that point (it's from the same window as the VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND-deprecation issue I found, so it's genuinely unclear without checking):

Your reference notebook sidesteps this entirely by using llama-cpp-python with a Q4_0 GGUF checkpoint, which runs natively on T4 without that attention-kernel problem.

There's one important catch before I rewrite this: your reference notebook only does text (no images). It explicitly excludes any GGUF file with "mmproj" in the name (find_q4_gguf filters those out) — mmproj is the vision-projector file needed for image input. Since your task is OCR (image → text), you'll need:

The same text GGUF your reference notebook uses (gemma-4-31b-it-qat-q4_0-gguf)

A matching mmproj GGUF (vision projector) for that same model — attached as a separate Kaggle dataset/input if you don't already have one

Good call switching — Qwen VL will also sidestep your original T4 problem directly, since Qwen's vision-language models use standard attention head dimensions (no 512-dim global-attention layers like Gemma 4), so you likely won't need the XFORMERS workaround at all.

Which Qwen VL model fits 2×T4 (30GB total VRAM):

Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct — dense, easily fits in fp16 on a single T4 even, fast, best default choice for OCR

Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct — MoE (30B total, ~3B active), needs a quantized checkpoint (AWQ/FP8) to fit comfortably across your two T4s, but stronger OCR/document understanding if 8B isn't accurate enough

Start with the 8B — it's specifically strong on OCR/document tasks per Alibaba's own benchmarks, and won't fight you on memory.

Two separate problems here, and the first one is more important than the OOM error itself:

Problem 1 (blocking): wrong model — no vision support

Your OCR cell loads QuantTrio/Qwen3.5-27B-AWQ. Look at the resolved architecture in your own error log: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration — that's Qwen3.5, the text-only successor line, not Qwen3-VL. It has no image encoder at all. Even if the OOM is fixed, this model cannot look at your scanned pages — llm.chat() would either error on the image content block or silently ignore it.

Your second (working) notebook uses this same text-only 27B model correctly — for a text hallucination-judging task with no images. That's a legitimate use of it. But copying its config into the OCR notebook carried the wrong model along with it. For OCR you need an actual Qwen VL checkpoint. I confirmed the real AWQ repo:

QuantTrio/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ

(30B total params, MoE with ~3B active — much lighter to run than a dense 30B despite the name, since only ~3B params activate per token.)

Problem 2: the OOM itself

Compare the two configs directly:

Failing (OCR notebook)
Working (judge notebook)

Your traceback shows the process had already burned 14.26 GiB of 14.56 GiB on GPU 0 before it even tried to allocate the KV cache. Weight loading alone was only ~9.9 GiB (same as the working run) — the rest went to CUDA graph capture, which enforce_eager=False triggers (CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, capturing dozens of graph sizes up to 512). On a T4 with only ~14.5 GiB usable, tensor-parallel graph capture across two ranks is exactly the kind of thing that eats the whole budget. Your working notebook explicitly sets enforce_eager=True for this reason and comments on it directly: "enforce_eager trades some speed for lower memory overhead... useful when VRAM is tight with a large model split across two 16GB cards."

Running in a subprocess matters too — your OCR notebook's main kernel had already imported sentence-transformers, faiss, bm25s, PyTorch, etc. in earlier cells for other work, leaving CUDA context fragmentation behind. A fresh subprocess with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set starts clean.

# %% CELL 2 — config (replace your MODEL_CONFIGS block)
MODEL_CONFIGS = {
    "qwen3vl_30b_a3b_awq": dict(
        model="QuantTrio/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ",  # <-- real VL model, not Qwen3.5 text
        quantization="awq_marlin",   # vLLM's own log suggested this over plain "awq" for speed
        tensor_parallel_size=2,
        max_model_len=8192,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.90,  # slight safety margin vs 0.96
        enforce_eager=True,           # <-- the fix for the OOM: skip CUDA graph capture
    ),
}
ACTIVE_CONFIG = "qwen3vl_30b_a3b_awq"
cfg = MODEL_CONFIGS[ACTIVE_CONFIG]

INPUT_ROOT = Path("/kaggle/input/datasets/mesbahuddinahamed/dl-corpus/corpus-pages")
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("/kaggle/working/transcriptions")
IMAGE_EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff"}
CHUNK_SIZE = 25
MAX_IMAGE_SIDE = 1600

OCR_PROMPT = (
    "This is a scanned page from a Bengali book. Transcribe ALL Bengali text visible "
    "in the image exactly as it appears, preserving line breaks and paragraph structure. "
    "Include any numerals, punctuation, and Bengali diacritics precisely. "
    "Do not translate, summarize, or add commentary — output only the raw transcribed text. "
    "If a region is illegible, mark it as [illegible] instead of guessing."

# %% CELL 3 — subprocess worker, mirroring your judge notebook's tp2 pattern
import subprocess, sys, pickle, os
from pathlib import Path

WORK = "/kaggle/working"

_OCR_TP2_WORKER_SRC = r'''
import sys, os, pickle, json
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image
from tqdm.auto import tqdm
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

def discover_images(root, exts):
    for book_dir in sorted(p for p in Path(root).iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        for page_path in sorted(p for p in book_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in exts):
            yield book_dir.name, page_path

def load_and_resize(image_path, max_side):
    img = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
    if max(img.size) > max_side:
        ratio = max_side / max(img.size)
        img = img.resize((int(img.width * ratio), int(img.height * ratio)), Image.LANCZOS)
    return img

def build_messages(pil_image, prompt):
    return [{"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "image_pil", "image_pil": pil_image},
        {"type": "text", "text": prompt},
    ]}]

def main():
    cfg = pickle.load(open(sys.argv[1], "rb"))
    outp = sys.argv[2]

    llm = LLM(
        model=cfg["model"],
        quantization=cfg["quantization"],
        dtype="float16",
        tensor_parallel_size=cfg["tensor_parallel_size"],
        max_model_len=cfg["max_model_len"],
        gpu_memory_utilization=cfg["gpu_memory_utilization"],
        enforce_eager=cfg["enforce_eager"],
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )
    sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=4096, repetition_penalty=1.05)

    output_dir = Path(cfg["output_dir"])
    exts = set(cfg["image_exts"])
    all_pages = list(discover_images(cfg["input_root"], exts))
    for book_name in sorted(set(b for b, _ in all_pages)):
        (output_dir / book_name).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def out_path(book, path):
        return output_dir / book / f"{path.stem}.txt"

    pending = [(b, p) for b, p in all_pages if not out_path(b, p).exists()]
    print(f"[worker] {len(all_pages)} total pages, {len(pending)} pending", flush=True)

    failed = []
    chunk_size = cfg["chunk_size"]
    for i in tqdm(range(0, len(pending), chunk_size), desc="OCR batches"):
        batch = pending[i : i + chunk_size]
        convs, valid = [], []
        for book, path in batch:
            try:
                img = load_and_resize(path, cfg["max_image_side"])
                convs.append(build_messages(img, cfg["prompt"]))
                valid.append((book, path))
            except Exception as e:
                failed.append((book, str(path), f"load_error: {e}"))
        if not convs:
            continue
        try:
            outs = llm.chat(convs, sampling_params, use_tqdm=False)
        except Exception:
            outs = []
            for c in convs:
                try:
                    outs.append(llm.chat([c], sampling_params, use_tqdm=False)[0])
                except Exception:
                    outs.append(None)
        for (book, path), result in zip(valid, outs):
            if result is None:
                failed.append((book, str(path), "generation_error"))
                continue
            text = result.outputs[0].text.strip()
            out_path(book, path).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

    pickle.dump({"total": len(all_pages), "pending_at_start": len(pending), "failed": failed}, open(outp, "wb"))
    print(f"[worker] done. {len(pending) - len(failed)} succeeded, {len(failed)} failed.", flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
'''

def run_ocr_subprocess(cfg, tag="ocr"):
    wdir = f"{WORK}/_proc_{tag}"
    os.makedirs(wdir, exist_ok=True)
    wpath = os.path.join(wdir, "worker.py")
    open(wpath, "w").write(_OCR_TP2_WORKER_SRC)
    inp, outp = os.path.join(wdir, "in.pkl"), os.path.join(wdir, "out.pkl")
    pickle.dump(cfg, open(inp, "wb"))
    if os.path.exists(outp):
        os.remove(outp)
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "0,1"
    print(f"[main] launching OCR worker (tp=2, both GPUs)...", flush=True)
    p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, wpath, inp, outp], env=env)
    p.wait()
    if p.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(outp):
        raise RuntimeError(f"OCR worker FAILED rc={p.returncode} — see subprocess output above")
    return pickle.load(open(outp, "rb"))

# %% CELL 4 — run it
worker_cfg = {
    "model": cfg["model"],
    "quantization": cfg["quantization"],
    "tensor_parallel_size": cfg["tensor_parallel_size"],
    "max_model_len": cfg["max_model_len"],
    "gpu_memory_utilization": cfg["gpu_memory_utilization"],
    "enforce_eager": cfg["enforce_eager"],
    "input_root": str(INPUT_ROOT),
    "output_dir": str(OUTPUT_DIR),
    "image_exts": list(IMAGE_EXTS),
    "chunk_size": CHUNK_SIZE,
    "max_image_side": MAX_IMAGE_SIDE,
    "prompt": OCR_PROMPT,
}
result = run_ocr_subprocess(worker_cfg, tag="ocr")
print("total pages:", result["total"], "| pending at start:", result["pending_at_start"], "| failed:", len(result["failed"]))
if result["failed"]:
    print(result["failed"][:10])

This keeps your original resumable design (skip pages with an existing .txt), runs entirely inside one subprocess so the model loads once and writes files as it goes exactly like your CELL 6 did, and streams tqdm/vLLM logs straight into the cell output the same way your working notebook did.

One more thing worth doing before committing to the full 776-page run: temporarily point input_root at a folder with just 2-3 sample pages, or add a [:5] slice on pending inside the worker, to confirm the VL model's Bengali OCR accuracy before burning GPU hours on all three books.

Good progress — the model swap, awq_marlin, enforce_eager=True, and the subprocess isolation are all correctly carried over. Two things left before this is actually runnable, though.

1. Two orphaned cells will crash

At the bottom of your notebook you still have the old validation cell and the old "build job list" cell from before we moved everything into the subprocess. They reference load_and_resize, build_messages, llm, discover_images, output_path_for, pending, all_pages — none of which exist in your main kernel anymore. Those functions only live inside the _OCR_TP2_WORKER_SRC string now, executed in an isolated subprocess. If you run those two leftover cells they'll throw NameError immediately. Delete both — CELL 4's printed summary (total, pending_at_start, failed) already replaces what they were doing.

(The duplicate config cell right after CELL 2 — the one that redefines cfg, INPUT_ROOT, etc. a second time with identical values — is harmless, just redundant. Fine to leave or delete.)

2. max_model_len=5000 is very likely too small — this is a real functional bug

You carried this value over from the text-only judge notebook, but that notebook never sent images. Here's the problem: your SamplingParams(max_tokens=4096) alone reserves 4096 of your 5000-token budget for output, leaving only ~900 tokens for the image + prompt combined. A 1600px-side scanned page gets tokenized into a substantial number of image patch tokens by Qwen3-VL's vision encoder — very likely more than 900 on its own. Requests will either fail outright or get silently truncated well before producing a full-page transcription.

Your original vLLM OCR script (before any of these fixes) used max_model_len=8192 for exactly this reason — worth restoring:

"qwen3vl_30b_a3b_awq": dict(
    model="QuantTrio/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ",
    quantization="awq_marlin",
    tensor_parallel_size=2,
    max_model_len=8192,          # <-- back up from 5000; image tokens + 4096 output needs headroom
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.90, # <-- pull back from 0.96 for a safer first run
    enforce_eager=True,
),

With enforce_eager=True you're no longer burning memory on CUDA graph capture, so there's real headroom to afford the larger context — this shouldn't reintroduce the OOM.

3. You've lost your pre-flight sanity check

The old validation cell (now deleted per #1) was genuinely useful — it let you eyeball OCR quality on a couple of sample pages before committing to the full 776-page run. Right now CELL 4 just processes everything pending. Worth adding a VALIDATE_ONLY flag to the worker so you can still do that cheaply:

# inside worker_cfg, add:
"validate_only": True,
"validation_per_book": 2,

# inside the worker's main(), right after building `pending`, before the chunked loop:
if cfg.get("validate_only"):
    per_book = cfg.get("validation_per_book", 2)
    seen = {}
    sample = []
    for book, path in pending:
        if seen.get(book, 0) < per_book:
            sample.append((book, path))
            seen[book] = seen.get(book, 0) + 1
    pending = sample
    print(f"[worker] VALIDATE_ONLY: sampling {len(pending)} pages", flush=True)

That reuses the exact same model/config/prompt path as the real run (so it's a true test of what production will do), just capped to a handful of pages — set validate_only: False once you've checked the printed output quality and are ready for the full corpus.

A few likely culprits, roughly in order of impact:

1. Check your model name vs. your config key — this might be the actual bug. Your dict key is qwen3vl_30b_a3b, which usually refers to the Qwen3-VL MoE checkpoint (30B total params, only ~3B active per token — comparatively cheap). But model= points at QuantTrio/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-AWQ, which is the dense 32B model — every parameter is active on every forward pass. On 2×T4 (30GB total), dense-32B-at-4bit is close to the ceiling before you've even accounted for the vision tower and KV cache. If you actually wanted the MoE variant, that alone would likely fix it — check for something like QuantTrio/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ on Hugging Face.

2. gpu_memory_utilization=0.98 is too aggressive on T4s specifically. T4s have no room for memory fragmentation slack, and vLLM's profiling pass (which measures peak activation memory to size the KV cache) can itself spike higher than expected with a ViT-heavy multimodal model. Drop to 0.85–0.90.

3. Cap concurrency and image size explicitly — for VL models, image tokens can balloon your effective sequence length well past what max_model_len suggests if you don't bound resolution:

max_num_seqs=1,  # or 2 — reduces reserved KV-cache/activation headroom during profiling
mm_processor_kwargs={"max_pixels": 1024 * 1024},  # cap image token count per Qwen3-VL's own knob
limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},

4. Drop enable_prefix_caching. It buys you nothing if each request has a different image (no shared prefix to reuse), and it reserves additional cache-management overhead. Set it False for this workload.

5. enforce_eager=True you've already got right — keep it, it avoids the CUDA-graph capture memory spike (same category of issue as your earlier Gemma 4 problem, though unrelated cause).

If you paste the actual OOM traceback (specifically whether it fails during weight loading, during the KV-cache profiling step, or on an actual generate call with a real image), I can point to the exact stage rather than the general list above.

"""
Bengali OCR pipeline using Gemini 3.5 Flash (Google AI API).

Same folder structure as before:
corpus_pages/<book_name>/page_NNN.jpg -> transcriptions/<book_name>/page_NNN.txt

Needs: pip install google-genai pillow tqdm
Needs: GEMINI_API_KEY set as an environment variable (or Kaggle secret).
"""

# %% CELL 1 — install
# !pip install -q google-genai pillow tqdm

# %% CELL 2 — config
import os
import time
import random
from pathlib import Path
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

from PIL import Image
from tqdm import tqdm
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

API_KEY = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY")  # or set directly / use Kaggle secrets
if not API_KEY:
    raise RuntimeError("Set GEMINI_API_KEY before running.")

client = genai.Client(api_key=API_KEY)
MODEL_NAME = "gemini-3.5-flash"

INPUT_ROOT = Path("/kaggle/input/corpus_pages")     # adjust to your dataset mount path
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("/kaggle/working/transcriptions")
IMAGE_EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff"}
MAX_IMAGE_SIDE = 1600          # same downscale guard as before
MAX_CONCURRENCY = 8            # parallel API calls (network-bound, not VRAM-bound)
MAX_RETRIES = 5

OCR_PROMPT = (
    "This is a scanned page from a Bengali book. Transcribe ALL Bengali text visible "
    "in the image exactly as it appears, preserving line breaks and paragraph structure. "
    "Include any numerals, punctuation, and Bengali diacritics precisely. "
    "Do not translate, summarize, or add commentary — output only the raw transcribed text. "
    "If a region is illegible, mark it as [illegible] instead of guessing."
)

GEN_CONFIG = types.GenerateContentConfig(
    # High-throughput extraction task, not reasoning — minimal thinking is
    # both faster and cheaper, per Google's own guidance for this use case.
    thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="minimal"),
)

# %% CELL 3 — helpers
def discover_images(root: Path):
    for book_dir in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        pages = sorted(p for p in book_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTS)
        for page_path in pages:
            yield book_dir.name, page_path

def load_and_resize(image_path: Path) -> Image.Image:
    img = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
    if max(img.size) > MAX_IMAGE_SIDE:
        ratio = MAX_IMAGE_SIDE / max(img.size)
        new_size = (int(img.width * ratio), int(img.height * ratio))
        img = img.resize(new_size, Image.LANCZOS)
    return img

def output_path_for(book_name: str, image_path: Path) -> Path:
    return OUTPUT_DIR / book_name / f"{image_path.stem}.txt"

def transcribe_page(pil_image: Image.Image) -> str:
    """Single call with exponential backoff for 429s / transient errors."""
    last_error = None
    for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES):
        try:
            response = client.models.generate_content(
                model=MODEL_NAME,
                contents=[pil_image, OCR_PROMPT],
                config=GEN_CONFIG,
            )
            return (response.text or "").strip()
        except Exception as e:
            last_error = e
            sleep_s = (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1)
            time.sleep(sleep_s)
    raise RuntimeError(f"Failed after {MAX_RETRIES} retries: {last_error}")

# %% CELL 4 — build job list (resumable)
all_pages = list(discover_images(INPUT_ROOT))
print(f"Found {len(all_pages)} total pages across {len(set(b for b, _ in all_pages))} books.")

pending = [(book, path) for book, path in all_pages if not output_path_for(book, path).exists()]
print(f"{len(pending)} pages remaining ({len(all_pages) - len(pending)} already done).")

for book_name in sorted(set(b for b, _ in all_pages)):
    (OUTPUT_DIR / book_name).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# %% CELL 4.5 — validation run on a small sample (do this before the full run)
VALIDATION_PER_BOOK = 2

sample_pages = []
for book_name in sorted(set(b for b, _ in all_pages)):
    book_pages = [p for b, p in all_pages if b == book_name][:VALIDATION_PER_BOOK]
    sample_pages.extend((book_name, p) for p in book_pages)

print(f"Running validation on {len(sample_pages)} sample pages...\n")
start = time.time()
for book_name, image_path in sample_pages:
    img = load_and_resize(image_path)
    text = transcribe_page(img)
    print("=" * 80)
    print(f"Book:  {book_name}")
    print(f"Page:  {image_path.name}  (resized to {img.size})")
    print(f"Chars: {len(text)}")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(text if len(text) <= 600 else text[:600] + " ...[truncated]")
elapsed = time.time() - start
per_page = elapsed / max(len(sample_pages), 1)
print(f"\nValidation took {elapsed:.1f}s for {len(sample_pages)} pages ({per_page:.1f}s/page, sequential).")
print(f"With MAX_CONCURRENCY={MAX_CONCURRENCY}, expect roughly {per_page * len(pending) / MAX_CONCURRENCY / 60:.1f} min for all {len(pending)} pending pages.")

# %% CELL 5 — run OCR concurrently
failed = []

def process_one(book_name, image_path):
    img = load_and_resize(image_path)
    text = transcribe_page(img)
    output_path_for(book_name, image_path).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return book_name, str(image_path)

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=MAX_CONCURRENCY) as executor:
    futures = {executor.submit(process_one, book, path): (book, path) for book, path in pending}
    for future in tqdm(as_completed(futures), total=len(futures), desc="OCR pages"):
        book_name, image_path = futures[future]
        try:
            future.result()
        except Exception as e:
            failed.append((book_name, str(image_path), str(e)))

# %% CELL 6 — report
print(f"Done. {len(pending) - len(failed)} pages transcribed successfully.")
if failed:
    import json
    print(f"{len(failed)} pages failed:")
    fail_log = OUTPUT_DIR / "_failed_pages.json"
    fail_log.write_text(json.dumps(failed, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"Details written to {fail_log}")

A few notes specific to this switch:

Cost matters now — you're paying per token instead of burning free GPU hours. Run the validation cell first and check the printed time-per-page estimate before committing to the full corpus; also worth checking current per-token pricing for gemini-3.5-flash since it's not cheap relative to 3.5-flash-lite.

thinking_level="minimal" is deliberate — Google's own guidance says leave it there for high-volume extraction tasks like this; raising it will slow things down and cost more without helping OCR accuracy.

Rate limits replace VRAM limits as your bottleneck — MAX_CONCURRENCY and the retry/backoff in transcribe_page handle that, but tune concurrency down if you hit persistent 429s on your API tier.

If accuracy on Bengali text disappoints, gemini-3.6-flash is now GA and generally stronger — same code, just change MODEL_NAME.

"""
Bengali OCR pipeline using Gemini 3.5 Flash (Google AI API).

Needs: pip install google-genai pillow tqdm
Needs: GEMINI_API_KEY set as an environment variable (or Kaggle secret).

# %% CELL 1 — install
# !pip install -q google-genai pillow tqdm

# %% CELL 2 — config
import os
import time
import random
import threading
from collections import deque
from pathlib import Path
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

from PIL import Image
from tqdm import tqdm
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

API_KEY = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY")  # never hardcode this — set it as an env var / Kaggle secret
if not API_KEY:
    raise RuntimeError("Set GEMINI_API_KEY before running.")

client = genai.Client(api_key=API_KEY)
MODEL_NAME = "gemini-3.5-flash"

INPUT_ROOT = Path("corpus-pages")     # adjust to your dataset mount path
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("transcriptions")
IMAGE_EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff"}
MAX_IMAGE_SIDE = 1600           # same downscale guard as before
MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE = 15       # hard rate limit
MAX_CONCURRENCY = 5             # worker threads; the limiter below caps actual call rate regardless
MAX_RETRIES = 5

OCR_PROMPT = (
    "This is a scanned page from a Bengali book. Transcribe ALL Bengali text visible "
    "in the image exactly as it appears, preserving line breaks and paragraph structure. "
    "Include any numerals, punctuation, and Bengali diacritics precisely. "
    "Do not translate, summarize, or add commentary — output only the raw transcribed text. "
    "If a region is illegible, mark it as [illegible] instead of guessing.\n\n"
    "If the page contains any embedded photograph, illustration, diagram, or other non-text "
    "visual content, do not attempt to transcribe it as text. Instead, insert a "
    "<figure>brief description of what the image depicts</figure> tag at the position "
    "where it appears in the page's reading order.\n\n"
    "If the page contains a table, reproduce it using Markdown table syntax "
    "(pipe-separated columns with a header separator row), preserving row order, column "
    "order, and every cell's contents exactly as written. Do not summarize, merge, or omit "
    "any table cells."
)

GEN_CONFIG = types.GenerateContentConfig(
    thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="minimal"),
)

class RateLimiter:
    """Thread-safe sliding-window limiter: at most `max_calls` per `period_seconds`."""

    def __init__(self, max_calls: int, period_seconds: float = 60.0):
        self.max_calls = max_calls
        self.period = period_seconds
        self.calls = deque()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def acquire(self):
        while True:
            with self.lock:
                now = time.monotonic()
                while self.calls and now - self.calls[0] >= self.period:
                    self.calls.popleft()
                if len(self.calls) < self.max_calls:
                    self.calls.append(now)
                    return
                sleep_for = self.period - (now - self.calls[0]) + 0.05
            time.sleep(max(sleep_for, 0.05))

rate_limiter = RateLimiter(MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE, period_seconds=60.0)

# %% CELL 3 — helpers
def discover_images(root: Path):
    for book_dir in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        pages = sorted(p for p in book_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTS)
        for page_path in pages:
            yield book_dir.name, page_path

def load_and_resize(image_path: Path) -> Image.Image:
    img = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
    if max(img.size) > MAX_IMAGE_SIDE:
        ratio = MAX_IMAGE_SIDE / max(img.size)
        new_size = (int(img.width * ratio), int(img.height * ratio))
        img = img.resize(new_size, Image.LANCZOS)
    return img

def output_path_for(book_name: str, image_path: Path) -> Path:
    return OUTPUT_DIR / book_name / f"{image_path.stem}.txt"

def transcribe_page(pil_image: Image.Image) -> str:
    """Rate-limited call with exponential backoff for 429s / transient errors."""
    last_error = None
    for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES):
        rate_limiter.acquire()  # every attempt — including retries — counts against the limit
        try:
            response = client.models.generate_content(
                model=MODEL_NAME,
                contents=[pil_image, OCR_PROMPT],
                config=GEN_CONFIG,
            )
            return (response.text or "").strip()
        except Exception as e:
            last_error = e
            sleep_s = (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1)
            time.sleep(sleep_s)
    raise RuntimeError(f"Failed after {MAX_RETRIES} retries: {last_error}")

# %% CELL 4 — build job list (resumable — only transcribes what's missing)
all_pages = list(discover_images(INPUT_ROOT))
print(f"Found {len(all_pages)} total pages across {len(set(b for b, _ in all_pages))} books.")

pending = [(book, path) for book, path in all_pages if not output_path_for(book, path).exists()]
print(f"{len(pending)} pages remaining ({len(all_pages) - len(pending)} already done).")

for book_name in sorted(set(b for b, _ in all_pages)):
    (OUTPUT_DIR / book_name).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

est_minutes = len(pending) / MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE
print(f"At {MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE} calls/min, the full pending run will take at least ~{est_minutes:.1f} min.")

# %% CELL 4.5 — validation run on a small sample (do this before the full run)
VALIDATION_PER_BOOK = 0  # set > 0 to sanity-check the new figure/table prompt before the full run

sample_pages = []
for book_name in sorted(set(b for b, _ in all_pages)):
    book_pages = [p for b, p in all_pages if b == book_name][:VALIDATION_PER_BOOK]
    sample_pages.extend((book_name, p) for p in book_pages)

if sample_pages:
    print(f"Running validation on {len(sample_pages)} sample pages...\n")
    start = time.time()
    for book_name, image_path in sample_pages:
        img = load_and_resize(image_path)
        text = transcribe_page(img)
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"Book:  {book_name}")
        print(f"Page:  {image_path.name}  (resized to {img.size})")
        print(f"Chars: {len(text)}")
        print("-" * 80)
        print(text if len(text) <= 600 else text[:600] + " ...[truncated]")
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    print(f"\nValidation took {elapsed:.1f}s for {len(sample_pages)} pages.")

# %% CELL 5 — run OCR, respecting the shared rate limiter
failed = []

def process_one(book_name, image_path):
    img = load_and_resize(image_path)
    text = transcribe_page(img)
    output_path_for(book_name, image_path).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return book_name, str(image_path)

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=MAX_CONCURRENCY) as executor:
    futures = {executor.submit(process_one, book, path): (book, path) for book, path in pending}
    for future in tqdm(as_completed(futures), total=len(futures), desc="OCR pages"):
        book_name, image_path = futures[future]
        try:
            future.result()
        except Exception as e:
            failed.append((book_name, str(image_path), str(e)))

    import json
    print(f"{len(failed)} pages failed:")
    fail_log = OUTPUT_DIR / "_failed_pages.json"
    fail_log.write_text(json.dumps(failed, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"Details written to {fail_log}")

What changed:

RateLimiter — a shared sliding-window limiter (deque of call timestamps + lock) that every thread calls into before hitting the API. It blocks a thread until a slot frees up rather than just sleeping a fixed interval, so it stays accurate even under concurrency. Retries also consume a slot, since they're real requests.

Dropped MAX_CONCURRENCY to 5 — with a 15/min ceiling, 8 idle threads mostly just wait; fewer threads is cleaner without losing throughput.

Prompt now tells the model to emit <figure>...</figure> placeholders for embedded images instead of trying to OCR them, and to render tables as Markdown tables rather than flattening them into prose.

The resumable pending logic is untouched, so re-running only processes images without a .txt output yet.

Worth running the validation cell (bump VALIDATION_PER_BOOK to 2 or so) on a page you know has a table or embedded figure before committing to the full run, to confirm the tagging behaves the way you want.

    "This is a scanned page from a Bengali book. Transcribe ALL Bengali text visible "
    "in the image exactly as it appears, preserving line breaks and paragraph structure. "
    "Include any numerals, punctuation, and Bengali diacritics precisely. "
    "Do not translate, summarize, or add commentary — output only the raw transcribed text. "
    "If a region is illegible, mark it as [illegible] instead of guessing.\n\n"
    f"If the page is entirely blank or contains no discernible text, figure, or table at all, "
    f"output only the exact string {EMPTY_SENTINEL} and nothing else.\n\n"
    "If the page contains any embedded photograph, illustration, diagram, or other non-text "
    "visual content, do not attempt to transcribe the image itself. Insert a "
    "<figure></figure> tag at the position where it appears in the page's reading order. "

    "has no printed caption at all, write a brief neutral description of the image inside the "
    "tags instead.\n\n"
    "If the page contains a table, reproduce it using Markdown table syntax "
    "(pipe-separated columns with a header separator row), preserving row order, column "
    "order, and every cell's contents exactly as written. Do not summarize, merge, or omit "
    "any table cells."
)

GEN_CONFIG = types.GenerateContentConfig(
    thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="minimal"),
)

class RateLimiter:
    """Thread-safe sliding-window limiter: at most `max_calls` per `period_seconds`."""

    def __init__(self, max_calls: int, period_seconds: float = 60.0):
        self.max_calls = max_calls
        self.period = period_seconds
        self.calls = deque()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def acquire(self):
        while True:
            with self.lock:
                now = time.monotonic()
                while self.calls and now - self.calls[0] >= self.period:
                    self.calls.popleft()
                if len(self.calls) < self.max_calls:
                    self.calls.append(now)
                    return
                sleep_for = self.period - (now - self.calls[0]) + 0.05
            time.sleep(max(sleep_for, 0.05))

class ApiKeyPool:
    """Round-robins across multiple API keys, each with its own rate limiter."""

    def __init__(self, keys: list[str], model_name: str, calls_per_minute: int):
        self.entries = [
            {
                "key": key,
                "client": genai.Client(api_key=key),
                "limiter": RateLimiter(calls_per_minute, period_seconds=60.0),
            }
            for key in keys
        ]
        self.model_name = model_name
        self._cycle = itertools.cycle(range(len(self.entries)))
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def next_entry(self) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            idx = next(self._cycle)
        return self.entries[idx]

    def generate(self, contents, config) -> str:
        entry = self.next_entry()
        entry["limiter"].acquire()
        response = entry["client"].models.generate_content(
            model=self.model_name,
            contents=contents,
            config=config,
        )
        return (response.text or "").strip()

key_pool = ApiKeyPool(API_KEYS, MODEL_NAME, MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE)
print(f"Loaded {len(API_KEYS)} API key(s); effective ceiling ~{len(API_KEYS) * MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE} calls/min.")

# %% CELL 3 — helpers
def discover_images(root: Path):
    for book_dir in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        pages = sorted(p for p in book_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTS)
        for page_path in pages:
            yield book_dir.name, page_path

def load_and_resize(image_path: Path) -> Image.Image:
    img = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
    if max(img.size) > MAX_IMAGE_SIDE:
        ratio = MAX_IMAGE_SIDE / max(img.size)
        new_size = (int(img.width * ratio), int(img.height * ratio))
        img = img.resize(new_size, Image.LANCZOS)
    return img

def output_path_for(book_name: str, image_path: Path) -> Path:
    return OUTPUT_DIR / book_name / f"{image_path.stem}.txt"

def transcribe_page(pil_image: Image.Image) -> str:
    """Retries up to MAX_RETRIES times total, rotating to the next API key each attempt."""
    last_error = None
    for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES):
        try:
            return key_pool.generate([pil_image, OCR_PROMPT], GEN_CONFIG)
        except Exception as e:
            last_error = e
            sleep_s = (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1)
            time.sleep(sleep_s)
    raise RuntimeError(f"Failed after {MAX_RETRIES} retries across rotated keys: {last_error}")

print(f"{len(pending)} pages remaining ({len(all_pages) - len(pending)} already done).")

for book_name in sorted(set(b for b, _ in all_pages)):

def process_one(book_name, image_path):

write_text() runs immediately after each page's transcription comes back — inside the worker thread, per page, not batched or deferred to the end. as_completed() just yields the futures in completion order for the progress bar; the write already happened before that future was marked done. So if you kill the run partway through, everything transcribed up to that point is already on disk, and the resumability check in CELL 4 (if not output_path_for(book, path).exists()) will correctly skip it on the next run.

A few things that could make it look like nothing's being saved, worth checking on your end:

Relative paths — INPUT_ROOT = Path("corpus-pages") and OUTPUT_DIR = Path("transcriptions") are relative to wherever the process's working directory is. If you're running this in Kaggle and expecting /kaggle/working/transcriptions, but the kernel's cwd is somewhere else, files are being written — just not where you're looking. Print OUTPUT_DIR.resolve() at the top of CELL 5 to confirm.

File browser not auto-refreshing — Kaggle's and Jupyter's file panels often need a manual refresh; the files can exist on disk before the UI shows them.

Ephemeral session storage — if this is an interactive Kaggle session (not a committed/saved run), anything under the working directory disappears when the session ends unless you explicitly save a version. Files were saved per-page during the run; they just don't survive past session teardown.

Exceptions swallowed too early — if write_text() itself throws (e.g., the book subfolder wasn't created), that's caught by the except Exception as e in CELL 5's loop and logged to failed/_failed_pages.json rather than crashing — worth checking that file if pages seem to be silently vanishing.

If you print output_path_for(book_name, image_path) right before the write, or just ls transcriptions/<book_name>/ mid-run from a separate terminal/cell, you should see files accumulating in real time. Let me know what you actually observe and I can narrow it down further.

Good — that explains it. Zero files with the progress bar still advancing to 5/776 means those 5 "completions" were failures being silently absorbed, not successes. Trace the logic:

for future in tqdm(as_completed(futures), ...):
    ...
    try:
        future.result()
    except Exception as e:
        failed.append((book_name, str(image_path), str(e)))   # <-- swallowed here, no print

as_completed() yields a future whether it succeeded or raised — tqdm's counter just tracks "how many futures are done," not "how many succeeded." When process_one throws (which happens if transcribe_page exhausts all 5 retries and raises RuntimeError), that exception is caught here and quietly appended to failed — which only gets printed in CELL 6, and CELL 6 never ran because you interrupted before the loop finished. So every page was failing, not saving, and you had no visibility into it until now.

Given MAX_RETRIES=5 with exponential backoff (~1+2+4+8+16 ≈ 31s of sleep before giving up), and multiple pages failing at almost exactly the 35-38s mark you saw — that's consistent with every single API call failing immediately (an auth/config error, not a transient rate-limit issue that backoff would eventually get past).

Not a concurrency bug — it's silent failures, and the mystery numbers (7, 121, 7) in your output are a clue you already have but didn't notice: those are the return values of Path.write_text(), which returns the number of characters written, from this line:

print(output_path_for(book_name, image_path).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8"))

7 chars is exactly the length of the string <Empty>. 121 chars is a real transcribed snippet. So those three printed lines correspond exactly to your three saved files — the print only fires after a successful write. tqdm reaching 7/776 counts futures that finished, whether they finished by succeeding or by raising an exception. Look at the loop again:

try:
    future.result()
except Exception as e:
    failed.append((book_name, str(image_path), str(e)))   # <-- no print here

4 of those 7 completed futures raised inside transcribe_page (meaning it exhausted all MAX_RETRIES attempts and gave up) — process_one never reached write_text() for those, so no file, no print. They got quietly appended to failed, which only gets printed in CELL 6 — and you interrupted before CELL 6 ran, so you had zero visibility into why those 4 failed.

Architected standalone script to identify and segregate blank pages for manual review.

Architected standalone script to identify and segregate blank pages for manual review.

"""
Find pages whose transcription is <Empty> and move them (image + transcript)
into a separate 'blank' directory for manual review, mirroring the original
book/page folder structure.

Run this AFTER the main OCR script has produced .txt files in OUTPUT_DIR.
"""

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

INPUT_ROOT = Path("corpus-pages")       # same as the main script
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("transcriptions")     # same as the main script
BLANK_DIR = Path("blank")               # where suspected-blank pages get moved
IMAGE_EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff"}
EMPTY_SENTINEL = "<Empty>"

def discover_images(root: Path):
    for book_dir in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        pages = sorted(p for p in book_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTS)
        for page_path in pages:
            yield book_dir.name, page_path

def transcript_path_for(book_name: str, image_path: Path) -> Path:
    return OUTPUT_DIR / book_name / f"{image_path.stem}.txt"

def is_blank(transcript_path: Path) -> bool:
    if not transcript_path.exists():
        return False  # not transcribed yet — leave it alone, not a judgment either way
    content = transcript_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    return content == EMPTY_SENTINEL

def main():
    all_pages = list(discover_images(INPUT_ROOT))
    print(f"Scanning {len(all_pages)} pages across {len(set(b for b, _ in all_pages))} books...")

    moved = []
    not_yet_transcribed = []

    for book_name, image_path in all_pages:
        txt_path = transcript_path_for(book_name, image_path)

        if not txt_path.exists():
            not_yet_transcribed.append((book_name, str(image_path)))
            continue

        if not is_blank(txt_path):
            continue

        dest_image_dir = BLANK_DIR / book_name
        dest_image_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest_image_path = dest_image_dir / image_path.name
        dest_txt_path = dest_image_dir / txt_path.name

        shutil.move(str(image_path), str(dest_image_path))
        shutil.move(str(txt_path), str(dest_txt_path))

        moved.append((book_name, image_path.name))

    print(f"\nMoved {len(moved)} blank page(s) to '{BLANK_DIR}/':")
    for book_name, filename in moved:
        print(f"  {book_name}/{filename}")

    if not_yet_transcribed:
        print(f"\n{len(not_yet_transcribed)} page(s) skipped — no transcript found yet (run OCR first):")
        for book_name, image_path in not_yet_transcribed[:10]:
            print(f"  {book_name}/{Path(image_path).name}")
        if len(not_yet_transcribed) > 10:
            print(f"  ... and {len(not_yet_transcribed) - 10} more")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Notes:

Moves both the image and its .txt into blank/<book_name>/, keeping the pair together — so when you're eyeballing the image to confirm it's actually blank, the model's <Empty> output is sitting right next to it for cross-reference.

Checks for an exact match on EMPTY_SENTINEL after stripping whitespace, matching how your prompt instructs the model to respond — not a substring check, so a page that happens to mention "empty" in its actual text won't get swept up by mistake.

Pages with no transcript yet are reported separately rather than silently skipped, so you know if you're running this before the OCR pass finished.

It's a genuine move (shutil.move), so corpus-pages/ will no longer have those images afterward — if you'd rather keep the originals untouched and just copy them out for review, swap shutil.move for shutil.copy2 in both spots and I can adjust it.

Since this changes what's on disk (moves files out of your source corpus), worth running it once on a small test book first to confirm the results match what you'd expect before letting it loose on all three books.

Architected local image detection to filter blank pages pre-API.

Architected local image detection to filter blank pages pre-API.

"""
Detect likely-blank scanned pages using pixel statistics (no API calls) and
move them into a separate 'blank' directory before you ever send anything
to the OCR API — cuts cost and gives you a pre-flight sanity check.

Needs: pip install pillow numpy
"""

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

INPUT_ROOT = Path("corpus-pages")   # same as the OCR script
BLANK_DIR = Path("blank")           # detected-blank pages get moved here
IMAGE_EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff"}

# --- Tunable thresholds ---
# A page is flagged blank if EITHER condition holds:
#   1. Its grayscale standard deviation is very low (near-uniform page — no
#      real content, just paper texture/noise).
#   2. Very few pixels count as "ink" (dark enough to be text/marks) relative
#      to the page area.
STD_DEV_THRESHOLD = 8.0          # grayscale std-dev below this = suspiciously flat
INK_DARKNESS_THRESHOLD = 140     # 0-255; pixels darker than this count as "ink"
INK_RATIO_THRESHOLD = 0.002      # flag blank if ink pixels are < 0.2% of the page

DRY_RUN = True   # set False once you've checked the report and are ready to move files

def discover_images(root: Path):
    for book_dir in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        pages = sorted(p for p in book_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTS)
        for page_path in pages:
            yield book_dir.name, page_path

def page_stats(image_path: Path) -> dict:
    img = Image.open(image_path).convert("L")  # grayscale
    arr = np.asarray(img, dtype=np.float64)

    std_dev = float(arr.std())
    ink_ratio = float((arr < INK_DARKNESS_THRESHOLD).mean())

    return {"std_dev": std_dev, "ink_ratio": ink_ratio}

def is_blank(stats: dict) -> bool:
    return stats["std_dev"] < STD_DEV_THRESHOLD or stats["ink_ratio"] < INK_RATIO_THRESHOLD

def main():
    all_pages = list(discover_images(INPUT_ROOT))
    print(f"Scanning {len(all_pages)} pages across {len(set(b for b, _ in all_pages))} books...")
    print(f"Mode: {'DRY RUN (no files moved)' if DRY_RUN else 'LIVE (moving files)'}\n")

    candidates = []
    for book_name, image_path in all_pages:
        stats = page_stats(image_path)
        if is_blank(stats):
            candidates.append((book_name, image_path, stats))

    print(f"Found {len(candidates)} candidate blank page(s):\n")
    for book_name, image_path, stats in candidates:
        print(
            f"  {book_name}/{image_path.name}  "
            f"(std_dev={stats['std_dev']:.2f}, ink_ratio={stats['ink_ratio']*100:.3f}%)"
        )

    if DRY_RUN:
        print("\nDRY_RUN=True — nothing moved. Review the list above, adjust thresholds "
              "if needed, then set DRY_RUN=False and rerun to actually move these files.")
        return

    moved = []
    for book_name, image_path, _stats in candidates:
        dest_dir = BLANK_DIR / book_name
        dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest_path = dest_dir / image_path.name
        shutil.move(str(image_path), str(dest_path))
        moved.append((book_name, image_path.name))

    print(f"\nMoved {len(moved)} page(s) to '{BLANK_DIR}/'.")
    print("Re-run your OCR script now — it will only see the remaining, non-blank pages.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

How it works:

std_dev catches pages that are basically uniform paper (scanner noise only, no ink at all) — real text pages have high variance because dark strokes against light background swing the pixel values a lot.

ink_ratio catches pages that might have a little texture/shading but essentially no actual dark marks — counts what fraction of pixels are dark enough to plausibly be text, and flags anything below a tiny threshold.

Flagged on either condition since a page could fail one check and pass the other depending on scan artifacts (dust specks, uneven lighting, etc.).

It defaults to DRY_RUN = True — it'll print every page it would move along with its actual std-dev/ink-ratio numbers, so you can eyeball a few of the borderline ones, tune STD_DEV_THRESHOLD / INK_RATIO_THRESHOLD if it's too aggressive or too lax, and only flip to DRY_RUN = False once the candidate list looks right. Run this before the OCR script so the pages never get sent to the API at all — that's the main win over the earlier post-hoc approach.

If you have any scans with large diagrams/figures but genuinely no printed text, flag that to me — figure-only pages could trip the ink-ratio check depending on how much of the page the image covers, and I can add a size-aware exception (e.g. only flag as blank if ink is sparse and scattered rather than concentrated in one region).

Yes — OpenCV is the more standard tool for this and handles a few things numpy-alone doesn't: proper Otsu thresholding (auto-picks the ink/background cutoff instead of a hardcoded magic number), morphological noise removal, and connected-component analysis to distinguish "a few real text blobs" from "scanner dust speckled everywhere." That last part matters a lot for scanned book pages, which often have dust/noise that a raw pixel-darkness count would wrongly count as "ink."

"""
Detect likely-blank scanned pages using OpenCV (no API calls) and move them
into a separate 'blank' directory before OCR — cuts cost and gives you a
pre-flight sanity check.

Needs: pip install opencv-python numpy
"""

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np

INPUT_ROOT = Path("corpus-pages")   # same as the OCR script
BLANK_DIR = Path("blank")           # detected-blank pages get moved here
IMAGE_EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff"}

# --- Tunable thresholds ---
MIN_BLOB_AREA = 15          # connected components smaller than this (px^2) are treated as noise/dust, not content
INK_RATIO_THRESHOLD = 0.002 # flag blank if real-content pixels are < 0.2% of the page
MIN_BLOB_COUNT = 3          # flag blank if fewer than this many real content blobs are found

DRY_RUN = True   # set False once you've checked the report and are ready to move files

def discover_images(root: Path):
    for book_dir in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        pages = sorted(p for p in book_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTS)
        for page_path in pages:
            yield book_dir.name, page_path

def page_stats(image_path: Path) -> dict:
    img = cv2.imread(str(image_path), cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE)
    if img is None:
        raise ValueError(f"OpenCV could not read {image_path}")

    # Otsu's method picks the ink/background threshold automatically per-page,
    # rather than relying on one fixed brightness cutoff for every scan.
    _, binary = cv2.threshold(img, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)

    # Morphological opening strips isolated single-pixel noise (dust, JPEG
    # artifacts) before we count anything as "content."
    kernel = np.ones((2, 2), np.uint8)
    cleaned = cv2.morphologyEx(binary, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, kernel)

    # Connected components: count distinct ink blobs above a minimum size,
    # rather than just raw dark-pixel percentage. A real text page has many
    # small blobs (characters); a blank/near-blank page has almost none.
    num_labels, _labels, stats, _centroids = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(
        cleaned, connectivity=8
    )
    areas = stats[1:, cv2.CC_STAT_AREA]  # skip background label 0
    real_blobs = areas[areas >= MIN_BLOB_AREA]

    total_pixels = img.shape[0] * img.shape[1]
    ink_ratio = float(real_blobs.sum()) / total_pixels if total_pixels else 0.0

    return {"blob_count": int(len(real_blobs)), "ink_ratio": ink_ratio}

def is_blank(stats: dict) -> bool:
    return stats["blob_count"] < MIN_BLOB_COUNT or stats["ink_ratio"] < INK_RATIO_THRESHOLD

def main():
    all_pages = list(discover_images(INPUT_ROOT))
    print(f"Scanning {len(all_pages)} pages across {len(set(b for b, _ in all_pages))} books...")
    print(f"Mode: {'DRY RUN (no files moved)' if DRY_RUN else 'LIVE (moving files)'}\n")

    candidates = []
    for book_name, image_path in all_pages:
        stats = page_stats(image_path)
        if is_blank(stats):
            candidates.append((book_name, image_path, stats))

    print(f"Found {len(candidates)} candidate blank page(s):\n")
    for book_name, image_path, stats in candidates:
        print(
            f"  {book_name}/{image_path.name}  "
            f"(blobs={stats['blob_count']}, ink_ratio={stats['ink_ratio']*100:.3f}%)"
        )

    if DRY_RUN:
        print("\nDRY_RUN=True — nothing moved. Review the list above, adjust thresholds "
              "if needed, then set DRY_RUN=False and rerun to actually move these files.")
        return

    moved = []
    for book_name, image_path, _stats in candidates:
        dest_dir = BLANK_DIR / book_name
        dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest_path = dest_dir / image_path.name
        shutil.move(str(image_path), str(dest_path))
        moved.append((book_name, image_path.name))

    print(f"\nMoved {len(moved)} page(s) to '{BLANK_DIR}/'.")
    print("Re-run your OCR script now — it will only see the remaining, non-blank pages.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Why this is meaningfully better than the pure-numpy version:

Otsu thresholding adapts per-image instead of using one fixed darkness cutoff across every scan — handles pages scanned at slightly different exposure/contrast without needing you to hand-tune a brightness number.

Morphological opening removes single-pixel noise before anything gets counted, so scanner dust doesn't masquerade as "ink."

Connected-component blob counting is the real upgrade — a genuine text page has dozens/hundreds of distinct character-shaped blobs, while a blank page with some dust has just a handful of tiny, disconnected specks. Counting blobs (not just raw dark-pixel percentage) is much harder to fool with noise than the std-dev/ink-ratio approach from before.

Still defaults to DRY_RUN = True for the same reason as before — check the printed candidate list against a few actual images first, tune MIN_BLOB_AREA / INK_RATIO_THRESHOLD / MIN_BLOB_COUNT if needed, then flip to live.

One thing to watch for with your book scans specifically: if a page has a large photo/illustration but very little actual printed text, blob-counting could misfire in either direction depending on how the image content breaks up under thresholding — worth checking a figure-heavy page against this detector before trusting it on all 776.

Then the second part of the code will work with trying all possible enhancements to the pages to see whether they perform better or not.

I am pasting a reference enhancing code and the corresponding output after running tesseract on it.

def to_cv(pil_img):
    return cv2.cvtColor(np.array(pil_img), cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)

def to_pil(cv_img):
    if cv_img.ndim == 2:
        return Image.fromarray(cv_img)
    return Image.fromarray(cv2.cvtColor(cv_img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))

def prep_none(pil_img):
    return pil_img

def prep_deskew(pil_img):
    cv_img = to_cv(pil_img)
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(cv_img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    _, binary = cv2.threshold(gray, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)
    angle = compute_accurate_skew(binary)
    if abs(angle) < 0.1:
        return pil_img
    h, w = gray.shape
    M = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((w / 2, h / 2), angle, 1.0)
    rotated = cv2.warpAffine(cv_img, M, (w, h), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
    return to_pil(rotated)

def prep_denoise(pil_img):
    cv_img = to_cv(pil_img)
    blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(cv_img, (3, 3), 0)
    return to_pil(blurred)

def prep_clahe_otsu(pil_img):
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(to_cv(pil_img), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=2.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    _, binary = cv2.threshold(enhanced, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)
    return to_pil(binary)

def prep_margin_crop(pil_img, margin_px=100):
    cv_img = to_cv(pil_img)
    h, w = cv_img.shape[:2]
    m = min(margin_px, h // 4, w // 4)
    return to_pil(cv_img[m:h - m, m:w - m])

def prep_stroke_repair(pil_img):
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(to_cv(pil_img), cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    _, binary = cv2.threshold(gray, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)
    kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (3, 3))
    closed = cv2.morphologyEx(binary, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)
    return to_pil(255 - closed)  # back to black-text-on-white for OCR

def prep_unsharp(pil_img, radius=1.5, strength=0.8):
    cv_img = to_cv(pil_img)
    blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(cv_img, (0, 0), radius)
    sharpened = cv2.addWeighted(cv_img, 1 + strength, blurred, -strength, 0)
    return to_pil(sharpened)

def prep_full_recipe(pil_img, book):
    '''Per-book targeted recipe, matching what's proposed in the A1 form.'''
    img = pil_img
    if book == "Bharater-Krishi-Babyasthar-Parichay":
        img = prep_denoise(img)
        img = prep_clahe_otsu(img)
    elif book == "Krishi-Bigyan":
        img = prep_clahe_otsu(img)
        img = prep_unsharp(img)
    elif book == "Krishi-Darpan":
        img = prep_stroke_repair(img)
        img = prep_unsharp(img)
    img = prep_margin_crop(img)
    return img

PREP_FUNCS = {
    "raw": prep_none,
    "deskew": prep_deskew,
    "denoise": prep_denoise,
    "clahe_otsu": prep_clahe_otsu,
    "margin_crop": prep_margin_crop,
    "stroke_repair": prep_stroke_repair,
    "unsharp": prep_unsharp,
    "per_book_recipe": None,  # handled specially below (needs book name)
}
best_ocr_fn = OCR_FUNCS[BEST_TOOL]

sweep_records = []
for _, row in tqdm(eval_sample.iterrows(), total=len(eval_sample), desc=f"Preprocessing sweep ({BEST_TOOL})"):
    img_path = page_img_path_for(row.book, row.page_num)
    gtp = gt_path_for(row.book, row.page_num)
    if not (img_path.exists() and gtp.exists()):
        continue
    pil_img = Image.open(img_path)
    ref = normalize_for_scoring(gtp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not ref:
        continue

    for prep_name, prep_fn in PREP_FUNCS.items():
        try:
            variant_img = (prep_full_recipe(pil_img, row.book) if prep_name == "per_book_recipe"
                           else prep_fn(pil_img))
            hyp = normalize_for_scoring(best_ocr_fn(variant_img))
            cer = jiwer.cer(ref, hyp) if hyp else 1.0
            wer = jiwer.wer(ref, hyp) if hyp else 1.0
        except Exception as e:
            cer, wer = np.nan, np.nan
        sweep_records.append({
            "page_id": row.page_id, "book": row.book, "prep": prep_name,
            "cer": cer, "wer": wer,
        })

sweep_df = pd.DataFrame(sweep_records)
sweep_df.to_csv("preprocessing_sweep_results.csv", index=False)
sweep_df.head()print(f"=== Preprocessing sweep results using {BEST_TOOL} (mean CER / WER, lower is better) ===\n")
overall = sweep_df.groupby("prep")[["cer", "wer"]].mean().round(4).sort_values("wer")
print("--- Corpus-wide ---")
print(overall.to_string())

print("\n--- Per book ---")
per_book_sweep = sweep_df.groupby(["book", "prep"])[["cer", "wer"]].mean().round(4)
for book in BOOKS:
    print(f"\n{book}:")
    print(per_book_sweep.loc[book].sort_values("wer").to_string())

Here's the notebook. A few things worth knowing before you run it:

Model bake-off (Part 1) — chosen from a fresh search of what's current as of Aug 2026:

Tesseract (ben) — your existing baseline, kept for a fair comparison point

EasyOCR (bn) — solid GPU-accelerated default

Surya OCR — actively maintained multilingual detector+recognizer

PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 — PaddlePaddle added explicit Bengali support in their Jan 2026 release; this is probably your strongest candidate

bbOCR / ApsisOCR — the BRAC University + Bengali.AI + Apsis pipeline, purpose-built for Bengali and published against historical/degraded scans specifically

Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (4-bit) — general VLM prompted as an OCR engine, fits one T4 comfortably

GOT-OCR2.0 — cheap general-purpose OCR VLM, included as a "does a generic model already do fine" reference point, not expected to win since Bengali isn't a primary training language for it

Each model gets a load/predict/unload triplet so only one sits in GPU memory at a time — this is what lets the 7B VLM coexist with the rest on a single T4.

Part 2 wires up your exact preprocessing sweep code, generalized so it runs against whichever model wins Part 1 (not hard-coded to Tesseract), plus a compute_accurate_skew implementation (Hough-line based) since your snippet referenced it without defining it.

Part 3 re-runs the winner (model × prep) on a disjoint held-out sample so your final numbers aren't overfit to the small bake-off sample.

Two things to flag honestly: I couldn't execute this notebook myself (no GPU or Hugging Face access in this environment, and Kaggle mounts aren't visible here), so treat it as carefully-reasoned code rather than tested code — and the paddleocr_vl_predict / apsisocr_predict wrappers are the most likely to need a small API tweak, since both packages' interfaces have moved fast recently; I left comments pointing at where to check if they error. Set DATA_ROOT at the top to your actual mounted Kaggle dataset path.

You were right to push back — I checked the actual PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 model card directly. Bengali is mentioned in the release notes ("language coverage is extended to include China's Tibetan script and Bengali"), but it's not in the model's own language tags (only English/Chinese/multilingual are listed) and none of their published benchmarks test Bengali specifically. So it's a real but unverified claim — I've demoted it to a "Tier 2 / exploratory" model rather than a confident pick, with that caveat spelled out in the notebook itself.

I revised the model set into two honest tiers:

Tier 1 — actual evidence of Bengali support:

Tesseract (ben) — baseline

EasyOCR (bn)

Surya OCR — checked their repo directly; Bengali is one of the languages explicitly named in their own benchmark suite, so this one's on firmer ground than I'd given it credit for

ApsisNet — the real package name is apsisnet, not apsisocr (my earlier guess was wrong). It's the recognition engine that bbOCR itself uses, purpose-built for Bengali only. One important correction: it's a recognizer, not a full-page pipeline — it needs pre-cropped line images, so I paired it with EasyOCR's detector to feed it crops. That's now correctly reflected in the wrapper.

Tier 2 — plausible but unconfirmed on Bengali, worth testing anyway:

PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 (demoted, see above)

dots.ocr (rednote-hilab, 1.7B) — claims strong results across "100 languages," small enough to be cheap to test

baidu/Unlimited-OCR (3B, the DeepSeek-OCR successor you mentioned) — tagged only "multilingual" with no language list; its output embeds <|det|>... markers that need stripping, which the wrapper now handles

Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (4-bit), GOT-OCR2.0 — kept as general-VLM reference points

The framing in the notebook is now explicit that if a Tier 2 model wins, that's a genuine finding (the claimed multilingual coverage actually holding up on Bengali) rather than something to assume going in — your own CER/WER numbers settle it either way instead of a model card's word.
